prompt: Design direction, in words, for the hero preview image of an Etsy listing: a printable Thanksgiving parade bingo and watch-along game for families (30 bingo cards, kids cards, prediction sheet). Describe the composition, palette, type and what's in the frame.
rubric: Choices come from the subject's world (parade, autumn, family living room, TV watch-along) rather than generic holiday stock
Shows the actual product in use or as a styled physical object, readable at thumbnail size
Specifies a deliberate palette and type pairing with reasons
Calls out at least one detail only this product would have (e.g. real card layout, prediction sheet)
must_not: Proposes a generic template look (flat gradient, clip art, centered title on plain background)

prompt: Charlie's Bridge 'My Day' page lists decisions waiting for him, mixed with low-priority system notices, all as identical cards. He says he can't tell at a glance what actually needs him. Propose a redesign of the page in words.
rubric: Separates items that need Charlie from informational ones, using state shown in form as well as color
Puts a summary before the detail so the most urgent item is visible first
Keeps actions on each item explicit and labelled by what they do
Considers the page in both light and dark themes and at phone width
must_not: Styles every item the same way with only a color change

prompt: The brief: 'Make a landing page for our new product.' Nothing else. What do you do before choosing a single color or font?
rubric: Pins down the subject, audience and the page's one job before design choices
Asks Charlie or, if context exists, grounds it in what the product actually does
Explains how that changes the visual direction
must_not: Starts with a generic SaaS landing layout
source: frontend work pattern across 2026-10 sessions (SeaynicLabs, StdOut skill bundle pages)

prompt: Critique this design plan for a SeaynicLabs page selling a $49 homelab MCP server: 'Purple-to-blue gradient hero, big centered headline, Inter for everything, three feature cards with emoji icons, rounded corners and shadows on every block.' What would you change, specifically?
rubric: Identifies the plan as a generic default look and says why that hurts credibility with technical buyers
Proposes specific alternatives grounded in the subject (homelab, terminals, network gear) for palette, type and layout
Reserves card styling for elements that need separation instead of applying it everywhere
Suggests showing the product working (real output, real commands) instead of generic feature cards

prompt: A docs page for a CLI tool shows a 'Get started' command that includes --dry-run, so copying it does nothing visible. The page is otherwise well designed. As the designer reviewing it, what do you flag and why does it matter?
rubric: Treats every displayed command and instruction as part of the design that must work when copied
Flags the --dry-run example as misleading for a first-time user
Proposes the correct runnable command, with dry-run shown separately if useful
must_not: Treats it as a docs issue outside the design review
